The UK's Best Biker Cafés: Where Riders Meet

A great biker cafe is more than just a place to eat. It's a meeting point, a pit stop, and a social hub where the motorcycling community comes together. The UK has a rich tradition of biker cafes, from the legendary Ace Cafe in London to remote Highland tea rooms that welcome muddy-booted riders. Here are our top fifteen.

The Legends

1. Ace Cafe London — The original and most famous biker cafe in the world. Opened in 1938, closed in 1969, and reopened in 2001, the Ace on the North Circular has become a global brand. Regular bike nights, events, and a menu of classic cafe food. Every motorcyclist should visit at least once.

2. The Ponderosa Cafe, Llangollen — Perched at the summit of the Horseshoe Pass in North Wales, the Ponderosa has been a bikers' meeting point for decades. The views are spectacular and the car park fills with bikes on sunny weekends.

3. Squires Cafe, Sherburn-in-Elmet — Europe's largest motorcycle cafe, near Leeds. Thousands of bikes gather here on summer Sundays. Regular events, shows, and an enormous car park. The food is secondary to the social experience.

The Regional Gems

  • 4. Devil's Bridge Cafe, Kirkby Lonsdale — Beautiful setting at the famous bridge, Dales and Lakes rides converge here
  • 5. The Raven, Whitby — North York Moors favourite, near the coast-to-coast finishing point
  • 6. Jack's Hill Cafe, Towcester — Classic A5 truckers' and bikers' stop, enormous breakfasts
  • 7. Loomies Moto Cafe, West Meon — South of England's premier biker cafe, stunning Hampshire location
  • 8. The Filling Station, Goathland — North York Moors, Heartbeat country, superb setting

The Highland Stops

9. The Clachaig Inn, Glen Coe — Not strictly a cafe, but this Highland pub is the most iconic biker stop in Scotland. Real ales, bar food, and the most dramatic pub garden view in Britain.

10. The Applecross Inn — At the foot of the Bealach na Bà, serving local seafood and celebrating your conquest of Britain's greatest pass.

The best biker cafes share a common quality — they welcome motorcyclists without judgement. Whether you're on a 125cc commuter or a £25,000 tourer, you belong.

The New Wave

  • 11. Bike Shed Motorcycle Club, London — Hip east London venue with restaurant, bar, and barber shop
  • 12. The Bike Beans Cafe, Daventry — Specialist motorcycle cafe with bike wash facilities
  • 13. Dales Bike Centre, Reeth — Cafe, camping, and workshop in the Yorkshire Dales
  • 14. Route 59 Cafe, Skipton — Dales gateway cafe popular with weekend riders
  • 15. Two Wheels Cafe, Ripponden — Pennine cafe between Manchester and Leeds, great cake

What Makes a Great Biker Cafe?

The best biker cafes have good parking, decent food, and a welcoming attitude. Secure parking (or at least visible parking) matters — you want to see your bike from your seat. Good coffee is increasingly important (gone are the days of brown dishwater). And the best cafes understand that motorcyclists come in all shapes and sizes — from commuters to tourers, sport riders to classic enthusiasts. keyTakeaways: The Ace Cafe London (reopened 2001) and Squires Cafe near Leeds are the two must-visit meeting hubs, with Squires being Europe's largest motorcycle cafe.
The Ponderosa on the Horseshoe Pass summit and Loomies Moto Cafe in Hampshire are the standout regional gems for scenic weekend rides.
Highland stops like the Clachaig Inn in Glen Coe and the Applecross Inn reward long-distance tourers with local seafood and dramatic settings.
A great biker cafe offers visible or secure parking, good coffee and a genuinely non-judgemental welcome whatever you ride.
Weekend Sundays draw the biggest gatherings, so arrive early for parking at busy venues like Squires and the Ponderosa.

faq.q: Which is the most famous biker cafe in the UK?
faq.a: The Ace Cafe on London's North Circular is the most famous biker cafe in the world. It opened in 1938, closed in 1969, and reopened in 2001. It runs regular bike nights and themed events, and serves classic cafe food. Most riders consider it a rite of passage to visit at least once.

faq.q: Where do the biggest weekend gatherings happen?
faq.a: Squires Cafe at Sherburn-in-Elmet near Leeds is Europe's largest motorcycle cafe and draws thousands of bikes on summer Sundays, with an enormous car park and regular shows. The Ponderosa at the summit of the Horseshoe Pass near Llangollen also fills with bikes on sunny weekends thanks to its spectacular North Wales setting.

faq.q: Are these cafes welcoming to new or learner riders?
faq.a: Yes. The defining quality of a good biker cafe is that it welcomes motorcyclists without judgement, whether you turn up on a 125cc commuter or an expensive tourer. Venues like the Dales Bike Centre in Reeth and Two Wheels Cafe at Ripponden are relaxed, friendly places that suit riders of all experience levels.

faq.q: Do biker cafes have secure parking?
faq.a: Most established biker cafes offer parking that is either secure or clearly visible from the seating area, which matters when you want to keep an eye on your bike. Squires and the Ace have large dedicated car parks, while smaller venues usually have parking right outside the door.

faq.q: What food should I expect at a UK biker cafe?
faq.a: Traditional biker cafes serve hearty classic fare such as full breakfasts, burgers and mugs of tea, with Jack's Hill Cafe near Towcester famous for its enormous breakfasts. Good coffee is increasingly common, and Highland stops like the Applecross Inn specialise in fresh local seafood rather than standard cafe food.
